1.title: Park cars face to face off
1.say: Drive the two cars nose to nose close but not touching. Turn both keys off and pull them out.
placements: good car with full battery → parked nose to nose facing dead car with fronts close but not touching (in the video: maroon red car)
dead car with flat battery → parked nose to nose facing good car with key off and dash dark (in the video: black car)
watch_for: if the thick jump cables cannot reach both batteries you parked too far apart so roll a little closer but do not let fronts touch.
if any dash lights or radio stay on a key is still on so twist both keys fully off and pull them out.
1.check_yourself: It should look like two fronts pointing at each other with a short walk gap and both dashes dark.
1.safety: Look all around for people and moving traffic before you roll either car.

2.title: Open hoods find batteries
2.say: Pull the hood levers and lift both hoods wide open. Find the black square battery box in each front corner.
placements: good car hood → lifted up and held open over front engine space (in the video: maroon car hood standing open)
dead car hood → lifted up and held open over front engine space (in the video: black car hood held open with wood stick on right side)
good car black battery box → inside engine space to one side near side wall (in the video: front corner of maroon car bay near headlight)
dead car black battery box → inside engine space to one side near headlight with little red cover over plus nub (in the video: front corner of black car bay)
watch_for: if you see a white plastic jug with a cap that is wash water not the battery so keep looking for the black box with two metal nubs.
if the hood feels heavy and will not stay up do not duck under it but fix the holding arm first.
2.check_yourself: It should look like both hoods standing wide open with a black box battery showing in each front engine space.
2.safety: Hold each hood wide until the arm locks so it cannot fall on your hands.

3.title: Clip red to plus posts
3.say: Bite the dead car end red clip onto the plus post of the dead battery. Bite the helper car end red clip onto the plus post of the helper battery.
placements: dead car end red spring clip on red cable → onto plus nub of dead battery usually marked plus or under little red cover squeezed tight (in the video: copper teeth on back nub of black car battery)

helper car end red spring clip on red cable → onto plus nub of helper battery usually marked plus or under little red cover squeezed tight (in the video: copper teeth on front nub of maroon car battery with red cover flipped back)
watch_for: if a red clip wiggles or pops off you missed the metal nub so squeeze open wide and bite down tight.
if both red clips sit on the same battery one end is on the wrong car so move one red clip to the other car plus nub.
3.check_yourself: It should look like a red clip biting the plus nub on each battery with the copper teeth tight and nothing else touching.
3.safety: Keep the loose metal teeth from touching each other or the car.

4.title: Clip black to minus and metal
4.say: Bite the helper end black clip onto the minus post of the helper battery. Bite the dead end black clip onto clean bare metal away from the battery.
placements: helper car end black spring clip on black cable → onto minus nub of helper battery marked minus opposite plus nub squeezed tight (in the video: rear nub of maroon car battery)
dead car end black spring clip on black cable → onto clean bare shiny bolt on dead engine away from battery squeezed tight (in the video: bare metal ring near front headlight of black car)
watch_for: if you clipped the dead car black clip to the dead battery minus nub move it to bare engine metal or sparks can pop.
if the clip sits on paint grease or rust wiggle to shiny bare metal until it holds tight.
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black clip biting the helper minus nub and the other black clip pinching clean bare engine metal on the dead car.
4.safety: Clip the dead car black clip to bare metal never to the dead minus nub.

5.title: Start helper car to charge
5.say: Sit in the helper car and turn the key to run the engine. Let it run a few minutes to feed the dead battery.
placements: helper car key in dash slot right of wheel → turned forward by hand until dash lights glow and engine hums (in the video: hand turning key in beige dash with red lights on)
helper engine → left running idle a few minutes to feed dead battery with hoods open and clips biting (in the video: both cars parked with cables on)
watch_for: if the helper engine stops right away you turned the key back too far so turn forward again to run.
if a clip pops off when the engine shakes push it back on to bite tight before charging.
5.check_yourself: It should look like the helper dash glowing with its engine humming while all four clips stay biting tight.
5.safety: Keep hands and loose clothing clear of the spinning fan and belts under the hood.

6.title: Start dead car remove cables
6.say: Turn the key in the dead car to run its engine. Pull the red and black spring clips off in reverse order. Let the jumped engine run a few minutes alone.
placements: dead car key in dash slot right of wheel → turned forward by hand until dead engine starts (in the video: hand turning key with orange dash needles lit)
dead car end black spring clip → lifted off bare engine metal first and held clear (in the video: hand lifting clip near black car headlight)
helper car end black spring clip → lifted off helper battery minus nub second (in the video: clip lifted off rear nub of maroon car battery)
helper car end red spring clip → lifted off helper battery plus nub third (in the video: clip lifted off front nub of maroon car battery)
dead car end red spring clip → lifted off dead battery plus nub last with all cables clear of metal (in the video: both engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear)
watch_for: if the jumped engine dies right after you pull the cables you did not charge long enough so put clips back and charge more.
if loose metal teeth touch each other while lifting you will see a spark so hold each clip alone away from metal.
6.check_yourself: It should look like both engines humming with no clips on either battery plus nub minus nub or metal and cables held clear.
6.safety: Lift one clip at a time without letting the metal teeth touch each other.
